newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta bourse ends lower, funds support lacking.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta bourse ends lower, funds support lacking.

text.p: Calcutta shares ended lower on Friday on low volumes and litte support from foreign and domestic funds, brokers said.
They said barring ITC shares, most other blue-chips tended to edge lower. State Bank fell sharply although this scrip was traded very heavily.

Bombay brokers said there were sellers in SBI after news the bank would launch its GDR issue this month. "There were some foreign funds selling with the intention of picking up stock from the GDR," one trader said.
Calcutta brokers said that neither foreign funds nor Indian mutual funds were finding anything interesting in the market.

"Retail investors are just not in the market. Just a handful of scrips are being traded while others were either not being traded nor getting quoted progressively at lower levels," said a dealer with brokers Ratnabali Securities Limited.
